set.approach: From the trailhead at the end of the long forest road out of the Slocan Valley (road condition varies from year to year), a well-graded trail climbs steeply through forest and then breaks out into open alpine. It leads to the camp area at the foot of the mountain, known as the Beach, which has an outhouse, and on to the toe of the South Ridge. The route starts at the toe of the ridge, left of the ledge where packs are usually left, on easy slabs that lead to a white corner.
set.descent_text: The last pitch of roped climbing ends on the lower south summit. A stretch of Class 3 ridge leads to a notch and then a short Class 2 scramble to the true, slightly higher summit. Once on the true summit, the way down is the East Ridge, which is steep Class 3 down-climbing on ledges, with a couple of steps many parties treat as 4th class. The most awkward move is right below the summit, and the ground eases lower down into scree, boulders and meadow. A cliff band low on the East Ridge cuts it off from the foot of the South Ridge, so parties who left gear at the base should plan how they get back to it; carrying packs and approach shoes up the route lets you rejoin the trail near camp.

review.notes: MP area + south ridge page: approach trail, 3rd-class east ridge descent, crux at the top, cliff band low; stevensong/chossclimbers agree on class 3-4 east ridge; Alpine Baking confirms tree then alpine trail and top-out on south summit.

set.approach: From the trailhead at the end of the long forest road out of the Slocan Valley (road condition varies from year to year), a well-graded trail climbs steeply through forest and then breaks out into open alpine. It leads to the camp area at the foot of the mountain, known as the Beach, which has an outhouse, and on to the toe of the South Ridge. From the base of the South Ridge, traverse east around the foot of the mountain and scramble up ramps of grass (snow earlier in the season) toward the upper east-facing basin. The route is on the shorter south-facing wall beside the East-facing couloir that separates the upper South Ridge from the main summit.
set.descent_text: The last pitch is easier ground up and left to the summit, with large loose blocks to avoid. The East Ridge descent starts close by. Once on the true summit, the way down is the East Ridge, which is steep Class 3 down-climbing on ledges, with a couple of steps many parties treat as 4th class. The most awkward move is right below the summit, and the ground eases lower down into scree, boulders and meadow. Every belay is bolted, so rappelling the route with two ropes is an option. A cliff band low on the East Ridge cuts it off from the foot of the South Ridge, so parties who left gear at the base should plan how they get back to it; carrying packs and approach shoes up the route lets you rejoin the trail near camp.

review.notes: MP route page gives access, finish at the summit and bolted anchors; Beach Break page confirms the same approach to this side.

set.approach: From the trailhead at the end of the long forest road out of the Slocan Valley (road condition varies from year to year), a well-graded trail climbs steeply through forest and then breaks out into open alpine. It leads to the camp area at the foot of the mountain, known as the Beach, which has an outhouse, and on to the toe of the South Ridge. The east face is reached the same way as Valhalla Gold: pass the foot of the South Ridge, work around to the east side, and go up the slabs to the base. Early in the season a snowfield can guard the start.
set.descent_text: The sixth pitch has an easy escape out left to the ridge, where gear belays are available. The route can be rappelled from every pitch with two ropes, and anchors on the climbing line are bolted. Alternatively walk the ridge to the summit and use the East Ridge descent: Class 3 down-climbing on ledges, awkward just below the top.

review.notes: Single new MP page for the route; approach is referenced to Valhalla Gold's page. Rappel statement from route page.

set.approach: From the trailhead at the end of the long forest road out of the Slocan Valley (road condition varies from year to year), a well-graded trail climbs steeply through forest and then breaks out into open alpine. It leads to the camp area at the foot of the mountain, known as the Beach, which has an outhouse, and on to the toe of the South Ridge. The trail passes the South Ridge start, runs close under the West Face, then dips on its way toward the col between Gimli and Niselheim. Do not follow the downhill section; instead head up and left to the start, just left of the more obvious cracks of Lusting After Women.

review.notes: MP route page location text; approach only because no source says where the route ends.

set.approach: From the trailhead at the end of the long forest road out of the Slocan Valley (road condition varies from year to year), a well-graded trail climbs steeply through forest and then breaks out into open alpine. It leads to the camp area at the foot of the mountain, known as the Beach, which has an outhouse, and on to the toe of the South Ridge. Keep to the main trail beyond the Beach and the southwest face, heading for the col into Mulvey Basin. Once the trail has dropped steeply and started to rise again, watch for a shallow corner crack in dark rock on the west face; the first pitch starts at its base.

review.notes: MP route page location text; approach only because the top of the route is not stated.

set.approach: From the trailhead at the end of the long forest road out of the Slocan Valley (road condition varies from year to year), a well-graded trail climbs steeply through forest and then breaks out into open alpine. It leads to the camp area at the foot of the mountain, known as the Beach, which has an outhouse, and on to the toe of the South Ridge. Keep going along the main trail toward the col into Mulvey Basin. The route follows an obvious vertical crack on the overhanging wall left of the Space Buttress, near that col.
set.descent_text: The route is descended by rappel, using bolt, hanger and tat anchors. Double ropes get you from the third station to a small ledge from which you lower off slung rock. Back-clip the ropes while rappelling so the stations stay reachable, and carry extra tat.

review.notes: MP route page: location and rappel notes. Single page for the route.
